_what: Where the LIVE tool keeps what the update machinery (ops/) reads. When a new version or a new tool goes live, change these paths if they move, and nothing else in ops/ needs to change. See ops/README.md, 'The contract'.
tool: Bristow-Hall Rule, C1021 starter with the v3.76 closers and damage grade (collection 105; port 1022)
_version_files: Files besides code that make a version what it is. When the last good version has to run (ops/run.sh), every file a person's commit changed since it (and no run wrote) is put back with its code; these are used only if that history cannot be read.
_calendar_rules: 8 November 2026 (1022, C1021): the rows the C1021 starter reads - FRED-scheduled releases need no rule (claims 180, Employment Situation 50, JOLTS 192, G.17 13, GDP 53); the S&P 500 at the NYSE close; the month-end averages (FEDFUNDS, GS10, GS1) on the first business day after month end at 4:15 PM ET; the Baa average read the 7th (rule_day7). The v3.76 starter rows (H.15 daily, Google, ETA 539 month, DFEDTARU, LAUS) left the page with it. The rules h15_week, h15_daily, fomc, daily_next_morning, utc_day_end, month_end_plus_21 and fred_every_day remain available.
_calendar_read_lag_min: 24 September 2026 (seagate-0924): minutes after the release's time before a row is due, where the tool reads a later post than the release. The state insured rates come from FRED's state release (469), posted the Friday morning after the Department's Thursday 8:30 release (FRED's stamp on 18 September 2026: 8:39 AM ET), so the row is due Friday 8:45 AM ET; the day shown stays Thursday. 25 September 2026 (ops-0924): the WEI is shown at the Dallas Fed's 11:30 AM ET and read 10 minutes later, after FRED's post (11:39 both Thursdays read).
_conditional_slots: C1021 (1022): none. The v3.76 sudden-stop rule (a morning run for Google searches while the S&P 500 was near its line) left with that starter; C1021 reads nothing that posts on its own clock between releases.
_fomc_source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, read 22 September 2026 (second day of each meeting; the statement at 2:00 PM ET). The Board publishes the next year's calendar each summer: add it here then. The notification says when the list is about to run out.
